Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment Moderate thermal day with sharp lapse rates, light winds, and widespread high cloud cover. No precipitation or overdevelopment; suitable for experienced pilots at most sites, though cloud cover may soften peak heating.

Site Breakdown

  • Kingsbury grade: Favorable. Good thermals but variable wind direction limits ridge soaring. Flying window 10am–4pm, peak w* 415 ft/min, thermal ceiling 6891 ft AGL. Sharp thermal caution (advanced pilots only).
  • Hallelujah: Marginal. Strong thermals but 100% high cloud cover may reduce heating; W winds support ridge soaring. Flying window 11am–4pm, peak w* 430 ft/min, thermal ceiling 8405 ft AGL. Sharp thermal caution (advanced pilots only).
  • Slide Mountain: Favorable. Good thermals with SE winds developing in the afternoon. Flying window 10am–4pm, peak w* 425 ft/min, thermal ceiling 6235 ft AGL. Sharp thermal caution (advanced pilots only).
  • McClellan: Favorable. Strong thermals, suitable SW–S winds through early afternoon. Flying window 11am–2pm, peak w* 486 ft/min, thermal ceiling 6574 ft AGL. Sharp thermal caution (advanced pilots only).
  • West McClellan: Favorable. Good thermals with on-direction WNW flow during peak heating. Flying window 1pm–5pm, peak w* 423 ft/min, thermal ceiling 5447 ft AGL. Sharp thermal caution (advanced pilots only).
  • Peavine Mountain: Marginal. Strong thermals but hazardous low-level shear and only a brief on-wind window. Flying window limited to 1pm, peak w* 448 ft/min, thermal ceiling 5499 ft AGL. Sharp thermal caution (advanced pilots only).
  • Rainbow Ridge: Favorable. Excellent E–NE ridge wind in the morning, strong thermals even under 100% high cloud; highest thermal ceiling. Flying window 9am–4pm, peak w* 441 ft/min, thermal ceiling 9195 ft AGL. Sharp thermal caution (advanced pilots only).
  • Duck Hill: Favorable. Good afternoon thermals with NW winds ideal for ridge soaring. Flying window 2pm–5pm, peak w* 436 ft/min, thermal ceiling 6499 ft AGL. Sharp thermal caution (advanced pilots only).
  • Daydreams: Unfavorable. No thermal activity (peak w* 0 ft/min); suitable for sled rides only. Light variable winds all day.

Hazards

  • Sharp thermals (lapse rate >8 °C/km) at all thermal sites — suitable for advanced pilots only.
  • Potential rotor turbulence lee of Peavine Mountain and Carson Range due to shifting wind directions.
  • Low-level wind shear at Peavine Mountain (peak layer speed shear 6 mph at 8,455 ft AGL).

Site Forecast ?Top of Thermals (PBLH) — height of the turbulent mixing layer; thermals typically reach this ceiling.
LCL (Lifted Condensation Level) — altitude where rising air reaches its dew point; theoretical cloud base.
Cloud Base — lowest model level with >10% cloud fraction.
w* — convective velocity scale; higher = stronger thermals (ft/min).
Cloud Cover — max cloud fraction over the column (0–100%).
Wind thresholds: orange = 12 mph, red = 18 mph.
